MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 5, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:02 p.m., on May 5, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 30, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 7:35 p.m.)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  Council Member Reardon

Staff Present:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: One Potential Case.

City Council Minutes  1  May 5, 2014
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with three City Council Members present. Council Member
Reardon and Council Member Ury were absent.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council held a prior Closed Session during which
they were updated on the ongoing process whereby the City and the Successor Agency to the
former redevelopment agency are attempting to get the monies owed from the State back to the
City and the Successor Agency. The State is very difficult to deal with and it doesn't appear that
they will be cooperative in returning the $1.3 million that staff has determined the City is still
owed. State representatives are not in agreement on that so legal counsel is preparing to
commence litigation which the City has done previously. Mr. Curley noted that the first lawsuit
resulted in the City getting what it was due, the threat of the second lawsuit got the results that
counsel and staff wanted and now the City is back in the situation where moving to litigate is the
only way that Mission Viejo will be taken seriously and get back the money that it is due.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim May 2014 as "Water Awareness Month"

  Mayor Kelley presented proclamations to William Kahn, El Toro Water District Director;
  Richard Fiore and Scott Colton, Moulton Niguel Water District Directors; and Dan Ferons
  Santa Margarita Water District General Manager.

P2.  Proclaim May 4-10, 2014, as "Wildfire Awareness Week"

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to OCFA Battalion Chief Ken Cruz.

P3.  Proclaim May 2014 as "Lupus Awareness Month"

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Shonte Perluss and Bridget Hood
  representing the Lupus Research Institute and Lupus LA.

City Council Minutes  2  May 5, 2014
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bob Hayes, M.V.: invited teens in the community to John Wooden's "Pyramid of Success"
presented by Craig Impelman on Wednesday, May 7 from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at City Hall. He also
announced that "42" is the Movie of Character for the month of May and it will be shown in the
City Council Chamber on May 18 at 2:00 p.m.

Dennis Lumley, M.V.: announced that the City will recognize veterans of the Vietnam conflict
on September 20, 2014. To support the event, the Elks Lodge is hosting a dinner-dance
fundraiser on June 7 and he hopes the proceeds will result in a $4,000 to $5,000 donation
towards the Vietnam vets recognition event. Mr. Lumley encouraged the Council and residents
to come to the event and advance purchase tickets are available for $25 each at the Elks Lodge or
at the Murray Community Center.

Pete Afrosiobi, M.V.: representing Mission Viejo Youth Basketball, he noted that they have a
difficult time finding basketball facilities within the city limits that are available and
affordable. He asked if the City can find some space to build a facility for the residents.

Dale Sandore, Lake Forest: stated that the new dog park is great and is one of the better things
the City has done. He noted, however, that there are a few problems including a very narrow
entrance from the street, a heavy gate and lack of water inside the dog runs.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Reardon and Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April 21, 2014, as
  presented.

City Council Minutes  4  May 5, 2014
 STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that today, the Supreme Court gave a green light (under the
Federal Constitution) to uphold the tradition of opening City Council Meetings with prayer as
long as no particular religion is endorsed. He noted that he and the City Clerk have discussed
revisiting the Council's original structure where community members of the clergy can be invited
to say a prayer at Council Meetings.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

10.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Schlicht

11.  Resolution in Recognition of the Positive Impact Proposition 13 has had on the State
  of California and to Affirm our Support for Proposition 13

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report and the Council discussed the proposal.

  Mayor Kelley expressed some concern with the adoption of a resolution that was not
  written by the City Attorney’s office.

  City Attorney Curley noted that he has reviewed the resolution and it is legally sound. He
  also reminded the Council Members that they need to be comfortable with language that
  comes from third parties.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  adopt Resolution 14-14 In Recognition of the Positive Impact Proposition 13 has had on
  The State of California and to Affirm Our Support for Proposition 13.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Reardon and Ury

City Council Minutes  5  May 5, 2014
 12.  Mission Viejo Nadadores Facilities Use Agreement

  Council Member Schlicht presented the report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the contract is seriously flawed and he questioned
  the insurance coverage requirement and the indemnity clause.

  Council Member Ury arrived at 7:35 p.m.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay provided highlights and
  clarification on the City's new agreement with the Nadadores. He noted that the contract
  was signed by the Mayor on May 1 and there were no changes to form and content after
  the Council approved the draft on April 21, 2014.

Council Member Schlicht announced that she received an email over the weekend that she
considers to be threatening and conspiratorial in tone, as well as misconstruing her questions to
the City Manager as an attack. She stated that each Council Member has a fiduciary
responsibility to the citizens and have taken an oath to uphold the laws. She noted that when a
resident has a question that she cannot answer, she will forward the inquiry to the City
Manager. She stated that when she read the terms in the new contract with the Nadadores she
sent out an S.O.S. because she could see the flaws in a 20 year-contract that she feels had no
Council discussion, input or oversight. Council Member Schlicht discussed the creation of the
last contract that is set to expire on June 30, 2014, and she provided background on the public
hearings and closed session negotiations that occurred on the subject in 1999. In comparison,
Council Member Schlicht stated that this year the Council played no role and the only meeting
on the matter was April 21, 2014, during which the Council would not allow any discussion on
the proposed contract and they accepted the staff recommendation that the Mayor sign the final
contract without it coming back for final approval by the entire Council and thereby eliminating
further public discussion. Council Member Schlicht said that the concept of public hearings are
for public input and transparency and the Council Members' duty is to the taxpayers, not to
protect the interests of a private entity, regardless of whom or what the entity is. She reminded
her colleagues that she had a legitimate concern with the City's policy and parameters to protect
the City but not a third-party user and she wanted to understand that better but didn't know how
to ask the question. Consequently a resident had similar questions which she could not answer
so she forwarded the inquiry to the City Manager. She stated that every Council Member needs
to understand the terms and conditions of the contract with the Nadadores and that it is obvious
to her that administrative staff does not like Council oversight and the Council majority
accommodates that philosophy. Council Member Schlicht expressed that she wants to know
what the liability exposure is on the Marguerite swim center and she noted that the new contract
refers to improvements identified in a pending master plan that has not been seen by the public
nor the Council. In response to her emails the City Manager, on April 21, produced a document
identifying costs to operate other swim facilities in the area. When she asked for backup
material to support those claims and then conducted her own survey, Council Member Schlicht
said that the comparisons presented by the City Manager were apples to oranges. For example,
in Irvine there were two swimming facilities (in comparison to Mission Viejo’s one) and all the
City Council Minutes  6  May 5, 2014
 facilities listed on the City Manager's report were open to the public and run by the respective
City government. She discussed Council Member Ury's response to one of the emails in which
he asked the City Attorney to place an item on a future Closed Session to discuss ending the
expenditure of any additional City resources on Council Member Schlicht' s inquiries and she
noted that she would provide copies of the emails for the public record.

Council Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at recent events including Bill Craycraft's
memorial service, the Rotary Club's Annual Prayer Breakfast, the National Day of Prayer event,
and the Wounded Warriors softball game. She announced that Dr. Frank Lieberman was
honored at this year's Arts Alive festival and that the Capistrano Unified School District will now
hold the annual Fun With Chalk event and their festival was held this last weekend as well. In
conclusion, Council Member Schlicht shared a quote from Mark Twain: "It is curios that
physical courage should be so common in the world and moral courage so rare."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury outlined his attendance at recent events including the Wounded Warriors
softball game and an event at the Latter Day Saints Church in Rancho Santa Margarita for youth
volunteers. He shared with the Council a thank-you poster that he received from the young
people who volunteered at the City's new dog park and he noted the irony that they thanked the
City. Council Member Ury stated that things like that make one excited about the future and the
youth that are about to come into leadership.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness discussed his attendance at the Wounded Warriors game and Arts
Alive where the common chalk art themes were Star Wars and sharks. He stated that the biggest
event was the Rotary's Prayer Breakfast where Mayor Kelley was the featured speaker. Mayor
Pro Tem Leckness noted that there were representatives of the clergy from many different
countries and religions and the variety of prayers were very powerful.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley commended city staff for an incredible job in pulling off so many large events this
past weekend. She discussed some of those events including the Rotary Mayor’s Prayer
Breakfast, 9th annual Children’s Environmental Fair, Earth Day and Arbor Day volunteer
planting and expo and Marine Day at Lake Mission Viejo. Mayor Kelley outlined her attendance
at a Casta del Sol forum where Council Member Ury, Robert Ming and Lisa Bartlett discussed
their candidacies for County Supervisor and she noted that it was an informative discussion. She
also attended Santa Margarita Water District’s Water Awareness Day which, she noted, was a
good way to bring recognition to the important commodity of water. Mayor Kelley outlined her
time spent at Arts Alive and a Vocational Visions fundraising event. She reminded residents of
the upcoming John Wooden’s Pyramid of Success program which will be held on Wednesday,
May 7 from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. and she noted that attendees need to RSVP. Lastly, Mayor Kelley
announced that this month’s movie of character, 42, will be shown on May 18 in support of the
City Council Minutes  7  May 5, 2014
 character quality moral courage and she shared a copy of the character program flier which
features Mission Viejo Deputy Adam Sandler.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:00 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, May 19, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.
